title: Relayable Action Stream — PRD sketch
content:
Goal:
Enable a streaming contract where the Hosted API can emit 'relayable action' frames that a client SDK (or intermediary) can choose to 1) execute immediately, 2) enqueue/defer for background processing, or 3) transform and forward to another execution endpoint. This is targeted at low-latency UX for tool-augmented responses while keeping server-side safety and observability.

High-level idea (sketch):
- Model responses are emitted as a sequence of frames. Each frame can be: text token chunk, structured result, or an action envelope (relayable action).
- Action envelope = {action_id, schema, hints, cost_estimate, auth_scope, preferred_execution_mode}.
- SDKs expose a small runtime that understands the envelope and exposes hooks for: run-now, run-later, sandboxed-simulate, or forward-remote.
- Hosted API keeps a short-lived action registry so actions can be resolved by action_id if the client asks for server-side resolution or replay.

Why this (user value):
- Faster perceived latency: UI can show partial result and concurrently start tool calls without waiting for full model finish.
- Flexibility: clients can choose local execution when cheap or route to a Dedicated/Private endpoint for data residency.
- Resilience: if a client disconnects, actions remain addressable (with TTL) for retries or server-side cleanup.

Key UX flows to support:
1) Live assistant that needs to call tools (calendar, search, code-runner) mid-stream: emit action frames as they are discovered; client shows placeholders and resolves them as results return.
2) Mobile app with low network: client defers tool execution to background when on metered network and later reconciles results.
3) Server-side orchestration: platform can replay action envelopes to Dedicated cluster for higher fidelity execution and attach results to conversation.

SDK Ergonomics (developer-facing):
- API surface: Session.stream() yields frames with types: 'text', 'structured', 'action'.
- Action object simple methods: action.execute(policy="run-now"), action.defer(ttl_seconds), action.serializeForRelay(target_url).
- Default policy = optimistic-local: try to run small actions in-process (via registered adapters), otherwise call service endpoints.
- Hooks: onActionDiscovered, onActionResolved, onActionFailed for telemetry and retries.
- Lightweight adapter interface so platform / customers can register local tool adapters (e.g., calendarAdapter, codeRunnerAdapter) and opt into sandboxed execution.

Safety & Security considerations:
- Action frames MUST include an auth_scope and optional redaction hints. SDK should not surface raw sensitive tokens; only action metadata.
- Server should sign action envelopes (HMAC) so clients cannot spoof replay to other endpoints without detection.
- TTLs and one-time-use markers for actions that touch PII.
- Audit logs: action discovery, attempts, results, and final bindings must be traceable for compliance.

Observed telemetry we need:
- action.discovered.count per session and distribution by type
- action.latency.* (time from discovery -> first resolution attempt -> final result)
- action.deferred.ratio (how often clients defer vs run immediately)
- replay.success/failure when platform replays to Dedicated
- SDK-level events: onActionExecuteError with error type and adapter id

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Server emits action frames in streaming responses with documented envelope schema (v0).
- JS/TS SDK implements streaming iterator and exposes action object with execute() and defer().
- Reference adapters for two toy tools: 'search-lite' (external api proxy) and 'calc' (deterministic op).
- End-to-end demo: Chat UI shows placeholders for actions, resolves them in parallel while stream continues, and reconciles final transcript with embedded structured outputs.
- Basic telemetry: counts and latency histograms in Console for first two weeks.

Non-goals for MVP:
- Full-blown distributed transaction semantics across multiple action results (we'll add later).
- Built-in RBAC for customer-owned adapters — initial adapter model assumes trusted local registry.

Open questions / TODOs (sorted):
- Envelope format: JSON-lite vs compact binary? Need telem size tradeoffs. (owner: Asha)
- How long should server registry retain action_id -> payload mapping? Default 1 hour? 24h? (SRE input)
- Signing model: platform signing vs per-customer key? (security)
- Backpressure model: if clients spam action execution attempts mid-stream, how to throttle or offer graceful fallback?
- Replay semantics: reconciling when action output differs between client-run and platform-run (deterministic merge rules?).
- Billing model: how to attribute tool execution costs (hosted tokens vs delegated endpoint usage)?

Implementation notes / engineering constraints:
- Serving runtime: action frames should be emitted without blocking the token stream; runtime should schedule action discovery as side-channel events from the generator.
- Storage: small key-value store with fast ephemeral lookups for action registry (redis-like) and automated TTL eviction.
- Backwards compatibility: support non-action clients — frames should degrade to embedded structured placeholders.
- SDK: streaming iterator must be compatible with node/deno/browser and support abort signals for canceling deferred executions.

Experiment ideas:
- 'Speculative-run' flag: allow SDK to pre-warm local adapter with predicted input to reduce latency on execute().
- 'Progressive-credentialization' where sensitive actions can request one-time short-lived credentials from the control plane at resolution time.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight to get team alignment on framing. Please annotate the Open questions and add links to related PRDs (streaming schema, toolcall-safety).
- Suggested next step: product + security + eng sync to pick TTL, signing approach, and initial adapter model.

Quick references / links to related notes:
- Prior streaming schema sketches: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Tool-safety playbook (draft): CONFLUENCE-2102
- SDK streaming iterator proposals: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/256

Unresolved UX detail (example):
- If an action resolves after the user has continued conversation and a subsequent model turn contradicts the action result, how do we present / surface corrections? (need product / UX brainstorm)

Last callouts:
- Keep envelope small and typed; we don't want large payloads emitted in-line frequently. Use references + on-demand fetch to attach large payloads.
- Focus first on low-risk, idempotent actions for MVP (search, math, non-PII lookups).

End of sketch.
